subject.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX

question: Should Windows session navigation hide all resolver-classified background sessions by default, with an opt-in Sessions-page view and only an explicitly active background chat remaining selectable?
rationale: This is an intentional UX and behavioral policy change across several Windows surfaces, not a purely mechanical correction; maintainers need to set the long-term visibility contract alongside the upstream Gateway presentation direction.

options.title: Approve the proposed policy
options.body: Adopt structured presentation metadata and hide resolver-classified background sessions by default while retaining the explicit visibility toggle and active-chat exception.

options.title: Keep all sessions visible
options.body: Retain the readable-title resolver but remove default background filtering so existing session discovery remains unchanged.

options.title: Defer to the Gateway contract
options.body: Pause the Windows consumer until the upstream session-presentation contract has maintainer-approved semantics for families and background state.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed policy
recommendation.body: Adopt structured presentation metadata and hide resolver-classified background sessions by default while retaining the explicit visibility toggle and active-chat exception.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the documented contributor for both the Windows implementation and the coordinated presentation-contract proposal, though broader current-main ownership could not be verified here.
